ecological_interpretation: The Palmer colony-count and chick-performance series identify short-term history dependence in breeder redistribution, but they cannot structurally identify whether that history is carried by local adult attendance/breeding propensity, net movement of mature birds, or first recruitment. Even imposing within-island conservation of mature-bird movement leaves a non-zero latent null space, and exact biologically admissible latent decompositions can generate identical observed breeder counts.

public_data_gate.historical_context: Palmer/Humble protocols annually banded approximately 1000 Adelie chicks and standardized searches for returning banded birds across all Humble colonies.
public_data_gate.current_public_tracking_scope: 2018/19-2024/25 GPS and dive-depth foraging tracks near Palmer Station; not a historical breeding-colony encounter history.
minimum_data_needed: individual ID x year x breeding colony x breeding status resight histories
or independent estimates of breeding propensity/nonbreeder attendance

claim_boundary: Do not name adult dispersal, breeding propensity, retention, or first recruitment as the unique carrier from breeder counts alone.
A significant past-performance bridge coefficient does not remove this structural confounding.
Literature can alter biological plausibility but cannot identify which carrier generated the Palmer count series.
The result does not imply all latent mechanisms are equally plausible; it states that the current observables do not uniquely distinguish them.
